risks.note: The BRSR discloses that manufacturing of solar panels accounts for 99.08% of turnover and that Solar Module (Non conventional Energy apparatus, NIC 35105) alone contributes 99.08% of total turnover. Essentially the entire business rests on one product line in one industry, so any demand, pricing or policy shock to Indian solar modules flows straight through. Read from the BRSR Section A products/services table, routed into the profile and registry bundles.

The BRSR states the contribution of exports as a percentage of total turnover is NIL and that the entity serves zero international countries, operating across 26 Indian states with no international plants or offices. There is no geographic hedge against a slowdown in Indian solar demand or a change in Indian renewable policy. Read from the BRSR Section A markets-served block.
risks.risk: Purely domestic revenue base with no export diversification

risks.note: Management repeatedly attributes demand to the Indian policy framework - the National Solar Mission, Solar Parks Scheme, Green Energy Corridor Programme, Renewable Purchase Obligations, competitive tariff-based bidding, COP26 Panchamrit targets, and participation in PM Surya Ghar and PM-KUSUM. The MD&A cautionary statement explicitly lists regulatory changes among factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Withdrawal or dilution of these supports, or of protection such as ALMM, would directly hit order flow.
risks.risk: Dependence on government policy and flagship programmes

risks.note: The Company is building a 4.5 GW solar cell facility and an 18,000 MTA aluminium frame unit at Narmadapuram, Madhya Pradesh (INA 4 and 5, described in the Corporate Governance Report as under construction), and states the entire 4.5 GW cell capacity is being established in a single phase rather than staged. It is also pursuing further ingot and wafer facilities. Single-phase commissioning of a first-time cell technology concentrates commissioning, ramp-up and demand-timing risk into one event.

Flagged in the BRSR material responsible business conduct issues table as a negative-impact risk: raw materials often have environmental and social externalities and can disrupt operations due to community protests, legal or regulatory action and increased cost of extraction; cases of child labour, forced labour or other human-rights aspects across the organisation may lead to statutory violations. The Company assesses suppliers' ESG performance considering country-, commodity- and sector-specific risks. Read from the BRSR table, which routed into the profile bundle rather than the risks bundle.
risks.risk: Supply chain management and raw-material sourcing

risks.note: The Corporate Governance Report states the Company's foreign exchange risk emanates from import of capital equipment, spares and other raw materials, and that hedging is decided case by case based on prevailing market conditions, period of exposure and amount involved, with no exposure hedged through commodity derivatives. With a large imported-equipment capex programme under way, currency and commodity moves are only discretionarily covered.
risks.risk: Foreign exchange exposure on imported capital equipment and raw materials, largely unhedged by policy

risks.note: The BRSR material issues table flags both Business Ethics and Transparency and Corporate Governance as negative-impact risks: delayed or inadequate disclosure of corrupt practices or anti-competitive behaviour may create regulatory, reputational and legal risk and lead to exclusion from contracts, raising the risk premium on debt or equity; a weak governance structure can lead to corrupt practices, damage reputation and employee morale, and cause investor mistrust affecting long-term financial health. Relevant given a promoter-concentrated board where the two executive promoter directors together hold roughly two-thirds of the equity.

The MD&A notes that geopolitical uncertainties and elevated commodity prices created volatility across global supply chains, cites downside IMF scenarios in which global growth slows to 2.5% or about 2.0% on energy-infrastructure damage, and records the RBI cutting its FY27 India GDP forecast to 6.6% while raising its CPI projection to 5.1%. Structural drivers are also said to face near-term challenges from interest rate movements, policy changes and global supply chain dynamics.

currentContext.expansion: FY2025-26 was the year INA stepped up a scale tier in module manufacturing. Through its wholly owned subsidiary Insolation Green Energy Private Limited the Company commissioned a 4.5 GW solar PV module manufacturing facility at Village Sawarda, Jaipur, Rajasthan (INA 3), lifting total installed solar module manufacturing capacity to 5.5 GW per annum alongside the existing Daulatpura (INA 1) and Jatawali, Chomu (INA 2) plants in Jaipur. The next leg is backward integration: the Company has embarked on a 4.5 GW solar cell manufacturing facility together with an aluminium frame manufacturing unit of 18,000 metric tonnes per annum at Mohasa-Babai, Narmadapuram, Madhya Pradesh (INA 4 and INA 5), described in the Corporate Governance Report as under construction, with the growth-journey timeline placing the 4.5 GW solar cell unit and Phase I 18,000 MTA aluminium frame production at 2027. Notably the entire 4.5 GW cell capacity is being established in a single phase rather than in stages, which management frames as a reflection of confidence in future demand and a commitment to rapid scale-up; the Madhya Pradesh work began on 45 acres of allotted land with other benefits. Beyond cells and frames, the Company says it is actively pursuing plans to establish solar ingot and wafer manufacturing facilities so as to create a fully captive ecosystem with 1:1:1 capacity alignment across ingots, wafers, cells and modules, positioning it among the few fully integrated solar manufacturers in India. The EPC vertical is housed under Insolation Green Infra Private Limited, incorporated in 2025, and 400+ MW of IPP projects are stated to be under execution. Management also notes evaluation of Battery Energy Storage Systems and other emerging clean energy technologies. The BRSR records 4 plants and 2 offices, all national, with no international locations.

risks.note: Management repeatedly attributes demand to the Indian policy framework - the National Solar Mission, Solar Parks Scheme, Green Energy Corridor Programme, Renewable Purchase Obligations, competitive tariff-based bidding, COP26 Panchamrit targets, and participation in PM Surya Ghar and PM-KUSUM. The MD&A cautionary statement explicitly lists regulatory changes among factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Withdrawal or dilution of these supports, or of protection such as ALMM, would directly hit order flow.

The Company is building a 4.5 GW solar cell facility and an 18,000 MTA aluminium frame unit at Narmadapuram, Madhya Pradesh (INA 4 and 5, described in the Corporate Governance Report as under construction), and states the entire 4.5 GW cell capacity is being established in a single phase rather than staged. It is also pursuing further ingot and wafer facilities. Single-phase commissioning of a first-time cell technology concentrates commissioning, ramp-up and demand-timing risk into one event.

risks.risk: Supply chain management and raw-material sourcing
risks.note: Flagged in the BRSR material responsible business conduct issues table as a negative-impact risk: raw materials often have environmental and social externalities and can disrupt operations due to community protests, legal or regulatory action and increased cost of extraction; cases of child labour, forced labour or other human-rights aspects across the organisation may lead to statutory violations. The Company assesses suppliers' ESG performance considering country-, commodity- and sector-specific risks. Read from the BRSR table, which routed into the profile bundle rather than the risks bundle.

risks.risk: Foreign exchange exposure on imported capital equipment and raw materials, largely unhedged by policy
risks.note: The Corporate Governance Report states the Company's foreign exchange risk emanates from import of capital equipment, spares and other raw materials, and that hedging is decided case by case based on prevailing market conditions, period of exposure and amount involved, with no exposure hedged through commodity derivatives. With a large imported-equipment capex programme under way, currency and commodity moves are only discretionarily covered.

The BRSR material issues table flags both Business Ethics and Transparency and Corporate Governance as negative-impact risks: delayed or inadequate disclosure of corrupt practices or anti-competitive behaviour may create regulatory, reputational and legal risk and lead to exclusion from contracts, raising the risk premium on debt or equity; a weak governance structure can lead to corrupt practices, damage reputation and employee morale, and cause investor mistrust affecting long-term financial health. Relevant given a promoter-concentrated board where the two executive promoter directors together hold roughly two-thirds of the equity.

The MD&A notes that geopolitical uncertainties and elevated commodity prices created volatility across global supply chains, cites downside IMF scenarios in which global growth slows to 2.5% or about 2.0% on energy-infrastructure damage, and records the RBI cutting its FY27 India GDP forecast to 6.6% while raising its CPI projection to 5.1%. Structural drivers are also said to face near-term challenges from interest rate movements, policy changes and global supply chain dynamics.

themes.title: Solar PV cell-to-module manufacturing
themes.need: Solar module/cell manufacturers ride capacity ramp, ALMM/DCR protection and an order-book build-out - a manufacturing thesis distinct from firm-power/FDRE tender economics or merchant storage arbitrage. Q1FY27 quantified the DCR arbitrage: EMMVEE grew revenue 51% to INR 1,555cr with EBITDA margin up to 35.2% and PAT +103% on a 9.9 GW order book, with DCR modules earning INR 8.5-9/W of EBITDA against INR 2-2.5/W for non-DCR - a 3-4x per-watt gap that structurally separates integrated cell makers from module assemblers. The offset is order timing: SWSOLAR booked a record INR 13,000cr unexecuted order value on a landmark USD 560m Egypt win (1,000 MW solar + 600 MWh BESS) yet revenue still fell 10% YoY, and flagged that industry orders concluded only ~INR 6,400cr against the >INR 20,000cr expected, deferred by DCR/module-price uncertainty.
themes.driver: DCR cell/module capacity commissioning and the ALMM List-2 per-watt spread; domestic ordering restarting after two slow quarters (SWSOLAR); order-book conversion.
